positions.commentary: Google's weakness has always been that they don't ship products, but they have lots of money and researchers.
Frederik Smith proved with FedEx that people will pay for instant delivery.
Amazon is excellent at fulfillment and can hold on for a long time as a reliable delivery mechanism.
eBay has amazing high gross margins but is the shittiest service in the world.
It's not clear that Microsoft has been able to preserve its advantage in business applications like Excel or Word over the last two years.
Devon is a save for banks because they won't need to attract talent and can use software to compete with software.
At PayPal, of the 254 employees when they went public, only two or three had any expertise in financial services.
At Airbnb, Brian, Nate and Joe did not have any hospitality experience.
Meta has cash and is trying to leverage it smartly, but they still need the ability to ship products.
Apple has the vertical integration required to build a device successfully, which no other company in the West knows how to do.

thesis: This episode argues that successful companies often emerge from founders with no domain expertise, relying instead on software and contribution-based metrics rather than traditional margins. It suggests that new entrants can disrupt established markets by creating instant delivery models and integrating software products with financial services, even in highly regulated environments.
